long_biography.plain_text:
Born Chan Kong-sang in Hong Kong, Jackie Chan entered the Hong Kong-China Opera Institute at seven. Over a decade, he studied acrobatics, kung fu and stagecraft. Early work as an actor and action choreographer led to breakthrough kung fu comedies in the late 1970s. There, he replaced imitation with a distinctive mix of danger, timing and slapstick.

That physical style became an international business platform. Chan carried it through Hong Kong productions and Hollywood franchises while taking producer credits, negotiating participation in films and licensing his name across cinemas, merchandise and endorsements. His role spans performance, directing, production and investment, with the screen career remaining the foundation beneath those extensions. An Academy Honorary Award recognized his lifetime contribution to cinema.
